title: Quiz Product and Teaching Proctor
description: Add the render-independent declarative quiz product (framework/products/quiz), the teaching domain with the proctor server (sqlite-backed CQRS/event-sourced user, run, score, badge and leaderboard tracking) and the first architecture/energy quizzes (physics, heating, cooling, energy demand) for quizze.architektur-und-technologie.de: onboarding (introduction, anonymous/pseudonym/name identity without password), randomized presentation, whole-run submission, partial-credit scoring with rank-distance metrics for numerical sortings, badges and a leaderboard. Reopened 2026-09-29: the UI becomes a card grid like semio-tech play and the mit-bestand demonstrator with the leaderboard as the central card; the proctor is zero-touch deployable on Docker under proctor.quizzes.architektur-und-technologie.de and the client is a static site distributed over a CDN at quizzes.architektur-und-technologie.de. Reopened again 2026-09-29: the quizzes page must be multilayered like semio-tech play — the content of every card rendered behind the glassy layer, and hovering a card shows its page clear. Reopened 2026-09-29 (night): presence shared within the quizzes — learners see what the others think (live draft answers, crowd of submitted answers, cursors on items); the home backdrop shows the real live subpages as a grid (presence inside them, live leaderboard). Reopened 2026-10-02 (overview camera): the overview of a quiz page is a 2D map of its pages whose camera follows the cursor in the background like semio-tech play and the mit-bestand demonstrator, with every page always visible in the overview. Reopened 2026-10-02 (crowd after submission): by default the results of the others show only after a quiz is submitted; the learner can explicitly ask to see the distribution before; everything about the others is plotted (answer distributions per item, score distributions). Reopened 2026-10-02 (overview exactly like play): two layers as on semio-tech play and the mit-bestand demonstrator — fixed cards on a grid in front, the screen-sized pages behind the glass; the background moves under the glass while the mouse is between the cards, and hovering a card brings its page to the screen, crisp. Reopened 2026-10-02 (overview frozen): the background must move between the cards also in the owner's Remote Desktop session, whose browsers report reduced motion.

summary: Built the render-independent quiz product (🧰️framework/🛍️products/❓️quiz: JSON Schema contract, TS + Rust twins of randomness, sheet, validation, scoring, badges, lifecycle and views; React renderer at 🎯️targets/⚛️react with local-first proctor client), the proctor server (🎓️teaching/🛂️proctor: Rust ServerInstance, CQRS + event sourcing over one SQLite file, API only, production gating) and the site quizzes.architektur-und-technologie.de (🎓️teaching/🏛️architecture/❓️quiz: catalog, 7 badges, Vite site, Dockerfile/compose/Caddy) with four sourced energy quizzes (physics, heating, cooling, demand). Scoring gives partial credit by magnitude-weighted pair concordance and profile similarity. Verified: nx tests of all 5 projects green, Protocol v2 parity 75/75 (numpy/scipy oracle vs TS vs Rust), taxonomy clean, Docker image build + check green, browser walk across two devices. Audits (spec, rules, content) found and fixed: leaderboard no longer publishes learner ids (tag), multi-tab data loss, cancel race, stale cross-device state, GEG 2024 labelling, score rounding, clipped radar labels. Shared fixes: framework CommandBus rehydrates actors after restart; ui-react i18n port split (site main chunk 1,691 kB → 414 kB); stale stash-pop conflicts in the repo library resolved. Revision 2026-09-29: the UI is a card grid in the semio-tech play / mit-bestand demonstrator language (WindowChrome cards, leaderboard as the central card, shared 🃏️OverviewCard for quiz, play and demonstrator, @semio-tech/ui-react/chrome); the site is a static CDN build for quizzes.architektur-und-technologie.de with the proctor origin baked in; the proctor is API-only and zero-touch on Docker (proctor + Caddy compose, baked production defaults, GHCR publish, manual GitHub Pages/GHCR workflow) at proctor.quizzes.architektur-und-technologie.de; shared presence: framework presence WebSocket with coalesced batches, quiz presence/cursor states in both cores, online roster, learning-now counts and live cursors anchored to shared cards. Verified: nx tests of 7 projects, parity 84/84, taxonomy clean (teaching, quiz, server), Docker image/stack checks incl. presence through Caddy, hub compiles against the framework changes, two-device browser check. Evening revision: the home is a layered overview like semio-tech play (shared 🥞️LayeredOverview element used by quiz, play and demonstrator; nine real pages behind one glass veil, hovering a card shows its page clear). Night revision: learners see what the others think inside the quizzes (thinking room with semantic live drafts, item/category cursors and drags, persisted CrowdView projection shown on quiz, run and results pages) and the home is a live grid of all nine pages (LayeredOverview grid rest, framework presence watch frame, others drawn inside every backdrop page, leaderboard and crowds updating live). Verified: nx tests of 7 projects, parity 93/93, taxonomy clean, hub compiles, two-device browser walk. Revision 2026-10-02 (deploy readiness): one dev command starts proctor and site (launch row 🛠️dev🏛️architektur-und-technologie❓️quizze); Playwright end-to-end gate in a dev and a cross-origin release-rehearsal topology; three audits (requirements, deployment/security, languages/accessibility) and their fixes: learner ids no longer readable through idempotency receipts, ids and handles validated by the server, per-address rate limits and caps sized for a lecture hall behind one address, sign-up allowance, bounded presence, scalable leaderboard (top 100 + own row), operator verbs health/backup/restore/erase/prune, capacity gate (300 learners beside an abusive script); distroless read-only image carrying its own stack files, hardened compose/Caddy/workflow, CSP on the site, readiness gate deploy-check, runbook; UI: no default language, accessibility fixes, honest identity wording, privacy notice and legal links, no layout shift from the crowd, typecheck gates. Nothing was published outward; the owner-only steps are in the site README. See 📓️closing-summary.md. Revision 2026-10-02 (overview camera): the quiz overview is a two-dimensional map of its pages whose camera follows the pointer in the background as on semio-tech play and the mit-bestand demonstrator, and no page ever leaves the view. Shared LayeredOverview: the grid rest gains a pointer camera (the map magnified about the pointer, pointerCamera; panZoom picks the largest magnification that keeps at least half of every page in view, 7/6 on the quiz desktop; props pan and panZoom, root attribute data-pan), reveals zoom from and return to the pointer's camera, and every follow is by elapsed time (followFactor), so the pan takes the same time at every refresh rate, also on the panorama of play and the demonstrator. Quiz: persisted local-only preference moveBackground with its switch in English and German and the note that a device asking for reduced motion holds the background still; home passes it to the overview. Fixture, schema, oracles d3-zoom and three (MathUtils.damp). Verified: layered tests 215 passed, quiz-react 498 passed with this revision alone (537 passed and 2 failed on the final tree, both in another session's navigation test file), typechecks clean, taxonomy clean, 14 of 14 mutants killed on isolated copies, end-to-end spec layered-home green in the dev topology and the camera test green in dev and rehearsal on the final tree (one test of another session's navbar work in progress failed there), measured in Chromium with normal motion. Finding: the workstation is a Remote Desktop session, so its browsers report reduced motion and the camera stays still there by design. Report 📓️overview-camera-report.md, design §19. Revision 2026-10-02 (crowd after submission, design §20, reports 📓️crowd-plots-report.md and 📓️crowd-distributions-core-report.md): by default the others' answers show only once the learner has submitted — on the results always, on a quiz's page once a run of that quiz is submitted, in a run only when the learner asks ('Show it now' / 'Hide it again'; ephemeral QuizState.asked, events crowd-asked / crowd-unasked, ends with the run); the persisted preference others (never | submitted | always) replaces showAnswers; crowdGate decides per place. Everything about the others is a figure: per task a table of small columns (rows = items, columns = categories, places or values; the share on the cap, the learner's own answer in the active colour with ●, the correct one with ✓ on results, a presence-coloured dot per learner thinking it now) and histograms of the scores of all runs (run, task, matching dimension) with the learner's own bin; new modules 📊️plot and a rewritten 🗳️crowd; the crowd lines under the items and the 'Everyone' column are gone. CrowdView carries the distributions: scores (ten bins) on the view and on every crowd task and places on sorting items, with scoreBin, placeBin and presented in both cores, numpy/Counter-corroborated vectors, the proctor tally keeping score bins and orders (PROJECTOR_REVISION 5). Verified: quiz react 613 tests and typecheck, quiz TS 297, quiz Rust 107, proctor 87 + 15 + 17, parity 108/108, taxonomy clean, end-to-end specs shared-presence and phone on a throw-away stack, screenshots from a private stack with the new proctor (crowd_plots_shots.ts). Not run: the end-to-end projects boot, desktop, shortage, pets and the rehearsal topology, blocked by other sessions' edits in flight (see the report). Revision 2026-10-02 (overview exactly like play; supersedes the overview-camera revision of the same day and the live grid backdrop of 2026-09-29): the quiz home runs the very mechanism of semio-tech play and the mit-bestand demonstrator — fixed cards on a grid in front, the nine real pages each as large as the screen on one strip behind one glass, the strip panning under the glass while the mouse is between the cards, gliding to the page of a hovered or focused card and showing it clear. The grid rest of LayeredOverview and everything that served it (props rest, gridTracks, panZoom; the per-page camera; LayeredRect, restRect, viewRect, coverPlacement, pointerCamera, panZoom and their vectors; the d3-zoom oracle) and the quiz preference moveBackground are removed. Kept: the pan follows by elapsed time (followFactor, judged against three.js MathUtils.damp), data-pan on the root, a warm pace of zero boots pages at once; home hands its card tracks to its stylesheet as --quiz-home-columns/rows. Verified: layered tests 142 passed, quiz-react 640 passed, typechecks and taxonomy clean, 10 of 10 mutants killed on copies, end-to-end spec layered-home 6 passed in dev and 6 in rehearsal, measured in Chromium with normal motion (the workstation's Remote Desktop session reports reduced motion, under which the overview neither pans nor glides, as on play). Report 📓️overview-camera-report.md, design §19. Revision 2026-10-02 (overview frozen): the overview's background stayed on the last page in the owner's browser because the workstation is a Remote Desktop session whose browsers report prefers-reduced-motion, and LayeredOverview's default reducedMotion="auto" switched pan and glide off for it. The element now defaults to reducedMotion="never" — pan and glide run whatever the device says, for the quiz, play and the demonstrator, as their original landings did; "auto" and "always" remain for an app that wants them. Verified in the session's own browser (data-pan pointer, the strip follows the pointer), layered tests 142 passed, quiz-react 640 passed, typechecks clean, 11 of 11 mutants killed on copies, end-to-end spec layered-home 6 passed in dev and 6 in rehearsal with the pan/glide test also run as a device that reports reduced motion. Report 📓️overview-camera-report.md §4, design §19.
